sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Plasma membrane localization confirmed by fluorescence microscopy (DPEP1-GFP at plasma membrane vs. cytoplasmic/nuclear GFP alone); enzymatic or receptor function NOT MEASURED in the tagged construct.
sites.rationale: DPEP1 is a GPI-anchored single-pass extracellular enzyme with signal peptide residues 1–16 (cleaved) and the entire mature chain (17–411) extracellular per the given topology. A C-terminal GFP fusion (pEGFPC2) is the only extracellular C-terminal position available; the paper explicitly names 'DPEP1-GFP' at the plasma membrane, so the junction is topology-derived at residue 411. Python confirms seq[410]='L' matching residue_before. No residue number is stated in the paper, so position_evidence is topology_derived rather than validated. Full-length DPEP1 cloned into pEGFPC2 (C-terminal GFP fusion vector), expressed in HCT116 cells; DPEP1-GFP localizes predominantly to the plasma membrane, confirming surface display of the tagged full-length protein.

sources.claim: While GFP alone was evenly distributed throughout the cytoplasm and nucleus, DPEP1-GFP localized predominantly to the plasma membrane, weakly in the cytoplasm, and strongly in an area consistent with the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) (Supplementary Fig.

literature_notes: L3 (Sino Biological DPEP1-Flag, HG13543-CH) was considered but disqualified: it is a commercial plasmid whose tag position is unstated, so insert_after_residue cannot be pinned. L5 (pcDNA3.1-Flag orthologs from pig, hare, cattle, dog) was considered but disqualified: tag position is unstated and the constructs are non-human orthologs with no residue named. L4 names both pEGFPN2 (GFP-DPEP1, N-terminal GFP) and pEGFPC2 (DPEP1-GFP, C-terminal GFP); only the C-terminal fusion is supported as a surface tag — the N-terminal GFP (pEGFPN2) places GFP before the signal peptide (residues 1–16), which would render it cytoplasmic or non-functional as a surface label, and L2 confirms only the C-terminal construct at the plasma membrane. DPEP1 is GPI-anchored; the C-terminal GPI signal (~residues 391–411) is normally cleaved during GPI attachment, so a C-terminal GFP fusion likely disrupts GPI processing — yet the paper documents plasma membrane localization, making this a published tolerated insertion that must be reported. The confidence is medium rather than high because the GPI biology complicates interpretation and no functional assay was performed on the tagged construct.

literature_other_positions.note: pEGFPN2 creates a GFP-DPEP1 fusion with GFP placed before the signal peptide (residues 1–16); GFP at this position would be cytoplasmic and not displayed on the extracellular surface, making it unsuitable as a surface tag.
